page: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is an arm64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 16 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model under the QEMU hypervisor. The system is equipped with 31.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.95 GB of memory per core, and includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position the cax41 primarily in the average tier for multi-core operations, while showing some weaknesses in single-core and specialized tasks. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 29117.84 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8500.0, both falling into the average category. However, single-core performance is weaker, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1052.0 and a weak Passmark memory score of 1828.1. Cryptography and text processing also show lower relative performance, as evidenced by a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 2590.29 and a weak Geekbench text processing score of 1200.0. Memory bandwidth remains solid, reaching 102.2 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and shared CPU model, the cax41 offers a cost-efficient option for parallelizable workloads that can leverage multiple Arm64 cores without requiring dedicated CPU execution. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 16.72 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 10852.79 on Passmark database benchmarks. Other appropriate workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and Redis key-value caching, where it handles 22.71 million SET operations per second. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks, heavy cryptographic processing, or large-scale LLM inference.
